stem: Select one entry from the choices that best completes the text.

content.text: Because the museum's collection is so {{1}}, spanning five centuries and thirty countries, visitors can spend days exploring it.

explanation: **Text Completion, one blank (five choices).** The clue is "spanning five centuries and thirty countries" and "days exploring": the collection is large and wide-ranging, *extensive*.

choiceExplanations.E: A collection covering five centuries and thirty countries is not narrow.
choiceExplanations.A: Visitors could not spend days on a tiny collection.
choiceExplanations.D: Spanning many countries and eras contradicts uniformity.

stem: Select the **two** answer choices that, when used to complete the sentence, fit the meaning of the sentence as a whole and produce completed sentences that are alike in meaning.

content.text: The shopkeeper was known for his {{1}} manner, greeting every customer by name and often offering a free sample.

explanation: **Sentence Equivalence (six choices, pick two).** Greeting everyone by name and giving samples shows friendliness: *genial* and *affable* give the same sentence.

choiceExplanations.B: Unfriendly, the opposite of the clue.
choiceExplanations.E: Someone who greets customers by name is not indifferent.
choiceExplanations.D: Self-important; not shown by the clue.

stem: For each blank select one entry from the corresponding column of choices. Fill all blanks in the way that best completes the text.

content.text: Although the novel was {{1}} on its release, it has since been {{2}} as a classic.

explanation: **Text Completion, two blanks (three choices each).** *Although* ... *since* marks a reversal. A book now treated as a classic was first *overlooked*, and is now *hailed*.

choiceExplanations.1A: Praise at release followed by praise now would not need *although*.
choiceExplanations.1C: Does not contrast with being hailed.

stem: Select the **two** answer choices that, when used to complete the sentence, fit the meaning of the sentence as a whole and produce completed sentences that are alike in meaning.

content.text: The committee's report was so {{1}} that it took readers weeks to understand even its summary.

explanation: **Sentence Equivalence.** "Weeks to understand even its summary" means very hard to follow. *Convoluted* and *abstruse* both capture that.

choiceExplanations.E: Enjoyable reading is not hard to understand.

stem: For each blank select one entry from the corresponding column of choices. Fill all blanks in the way that best completes the text.

content.text: A skilled reader does not {{1}} absorb a text; instead she {{2}} it as she goes, building a picture of the whole and {{3}} it when new information demands.

explanation: **Text Completion, three blanks.** *Does not ___ absorb ... instead* contrasts with active work: *passively*. Active reading is *interpreting*, and a picture of the whole is *revised* when new information arrives.

choiceExplanations.1B: Hurry is not the contrast with active reading.
choiceExplanations.2C: Ignoring the text is not building a picture of it.
choiceExplanations.3C: New information demands change, not approval.
choiceExplanations.3B: Copying the picture does not respond to new information.

stem: Select the **two** answer choices that, when used to complete the sentence, fit the meaning of the sentence as a whole and produce completed sentences that are alike in meaning.

content.text: The reviewer's praise was {{1}}, offered only after she had listed so many reservations that readers wondered whether she liked the book at all.

explanation: **Sentence Equivalence.** Praise surrounded by reservations is given unwillingly: *grudging* and *reluctant*.

choiceExplanations.A: Gushing praise would not follow a list of reservations.
choiceExplanations.F: Concerns timing; the clue is about unwillingness.
choiceExplanations.D: Praise offered only after a list of reservations is not spontaneous.
choiceExplanations.B: Poetic praise is not what the clue describes.

stem: For each blank select one entry from the corresponding column of choices. Fill all blanks in the way that best completes the text.

content.text: Scholars who treat the diary as straightforward {{1}} overlook that its author wrote with an eye to posterity, so that its apparent candor may itself be a {{2}}.

explanation: **Text Completion, two blanks.** Scholars who see the diary as plain *documentation* overlook that it was written for future readers, so the candor may be a *pose*.

choiceExplanations.1A: Scholars who saw it as a lie would not be overlooking the author's eye on posterity.
choiceExplanations.2B: A mistake, not something staged for posterity.
choiceExplanations.2C: A surviving object, not a feature of its tone.

stem: Select the **two** answer choices that, when used to complete the sentence, fit the meaning of the sentence as a whole and produce completed sentences that are alike in meaning.

content.text: Though the senator was {{1}} in public, rarely disclosing her intentions even to allies, her private correspondence reveals a woman of strong and often blunt opinions.

explanation: **Sentence Equivalence.** *Though* contrasts public restraint ("rarely disclosing her intentions") with private bluntness. *Reticent* and *guarded* both mean reluctant to reveal.

stem: The author mentions the netting experiments primarily in order to

choices.text: offer evidence that shorebirds help sustain the habitat in which they feed
refute the claim that mudflats look barren at low tide
recommend netting as a conservation technique
demonstrate that mudflats are more productive than other habitats
show that mudflat algae depend entirely on nutrients delivered by tides

explanation: **Reading Comprehension, select one (five choices).** The experiments are introduced after "Some ecologists once assumed ..."; where birds were excluded the algae thinned, "implying that the birds' probing and trampling help keep the system healthy".

choiceExplanations.E: The tides' nutrients are mentioned earlier; the experiments concern the birds.
choiceExplanations.D: No comparison with other habitats is made.
choiceExplanations.C: Netting was an experimental tool to exclude birds, not a recommendation.
choiceExplanations.B: The barren look is only a contrast with productivity.

stem: Select the sentence in which the author reports a view that the passage goes on to challenge.

answer.sentence: Some ecologists once assumed that the birds merely exploited a resource that would have flourished without them.

explanation: **Reading Comprehension, select in passage.** The sentence reports an earlier assumption ("once assumed"); the next sentence begins the challenge ("Recent field experiments suggest otherwise"). Other sentences state the author's own claims.

stem: Consider each of the choices separately and select all that apply. According to the passage, which of the following are features of the compromise approach to restoration?

choices.text: New paint is applied only where the original design is certain.
The new paint can be distinguished from the original on close inspection.
The new paint remains clearly visible at normal viewing distance.

explanation: **Reading Comprehension, select one or more (three choices).** The passage says new paint goes only "where the original design is certain" and "can be distinguished on close inspection". No partial credit: both correct choices are required.

choiceExplanations.C: The passage says the new paint "disappears at normal viewing distance".

stem: The last sentence of the passage serves primarily to

choices.text: summarize the dilemma presented at the start of the passage
concede that the critics' objection is correct
answer the criticism described in the preceding sentence
introduce a new example of a restoration that failed
propose an alternative to the compromise approach

explanation: The preceding sentence gives critics' objection; the last sentence begins "Supporters reply", so it responds to that objection.

choiceExplanations.B: Supporters *reply*, which is not a concession.
choiceExplanations.E: The supporters defend the compromise approach.
